summary: The migration of customer profile data from PostgreSQL to MongoDB aims to unlock flexibility for international expansion, eliminating schema limitations and reducing engineering overhead. A zero-downtime rollout with CDC-based backfill and dual-write infrastructure ensures data parity and backward-compatible APIs. The initiative prioritizes scalability, compliance with diverse country requirements, and improved performance (<50ms latency) while containing infrastructure costs to ~$5,000/month.
scope_overview: The release covers full migration of ~2M customer records (150GB) from PostgreSQL to MongoDB, implementation of CDC pipelines for live synchronization, adoption of a dual-write strategy with feature flags for zero downtime, parity validation, and rollback automation. Deliverables include new MongoDB schema design, indexing optimization, API compatibility assurance, and security compliance validations. Front-end remains unchanged.
key_risks: CDC pipeline latency may exceed 1s, risking data parity inconsistencies during rollout.
Schema mismatch or mapping errors could cause regulatory data loss or compliance issues in new markets.
test_readiness: QA automation is fully designed with 90%+ code coverage goals across unit, integration, and E2E tests. Performance tests confirm MongoDB meets <50ms p95 latency under simulated load, and rollback procedures are validated via CI/CD pipelines. CDC and dual-write behaviors are covered in integration scenarios ensuring sub-second synchronization and parity confirmation.
recommendations: Monitor CDC latency closely during the dual-write phase; scale connectors if delays approach threshold.
Conduct full-load dry-run migration in staging with parity reporting before production rollout.
next_steps: Finalize MongoDB index tuning and complete CDC connector setup within first sprint week.
Initiate dual-write rollout with real-time metrics monitoring and execute parity validation before final cutover.
